issues.title: Uniform Slater proof swaps the violating-index quantifiers

diagnostic_evidence.quote: for every $z \in \cS$, one can find a point $y \in \cY$ (possibly depending on $z$) satisfying $\bc(y, z) \leq -\zeta$.

issues.failure_explanation: The theorem has quantifier pattern “there exists ζ, for every z there exists y satisfying every component.” Its negation yields sequences for which, for every k and every y, there exists a possibly varying violating component. Equation bc-ineq1 instead assumes a single j satisfying the violation for all y and k. Finiteness of m does not justify moving that existential quantifier across the quantifiers over y and k, so the ensuing one-component MFCQ contradiction does not prove uniform vector feasibility.
issues.overall_effect: The old source does not establish the uniform Slater constant used to obtain uniform multiplier bounds. Consequently, the subsolver-rate and outer complexity chains depending on those bounds are unsupported until this proof gap is repaired.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Negate the vector conclusion without selecting a component in advance: take ζ_k decreasing to zero and z^k in S such that, for every y in Y, some component of bar c(y,z^k) exceeds −ζ_k, and pass to a subsequence z^k converging to z. MFCQ at z supplies a direction negative for every active constraint; a sufficiently small convex step from z in that direction makes all active surrogate components strictly negative, while the inactive components remain strictly negative by continuity. Fixing this point y, continuity and ζ_k tending to zero give bar c(y,z^k) ≤ −ζ_k for all sufficiently large k, a contradiction. This establishes the same uniform Slater constant, so the multiplier bounds and all dependent convergence and complexity results remain unchanged.
issues.why_classification: The quantifier exchange is a genuine proof error, not a transcriptional typo. Nevertheless, it is resolved by a short, standard local compactness-and-MFCQ argument using only ingredients already present in the theorem. No new assumption, auxiliary lemma, proof architecture, or weakening of any dependent guarantee is required, so the complete repair is minor.

issues.title: Missing subdifferential invalidates the stationarity-propagation lemma
issues.failure_explanation: Lemma lem:subsolver_output assumes that preceding iterates belong to the complement defined at X-eps and needs this to place the relevant iterates in U-eps, so that the local KL and growth estimates apply. Under the old formula, exclusion is governed by dist(0,Ψ(x)), which measures the scalar objective value rather than dist(0,∂Ψ(x)); no assumption relates these quantities. Hence the lemma's required nonstationarity premise is not established.
issues.overall_effect: The segment inclusion in U-eps, the local upper model Fstar-bound, and the inner-accuracy induction are unjustified. This leaves the general convergence lemma and the iteration and oracle complexity guarantees unsupported, although the executable algorithmic updates themselves are unchanged.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Insert the missing subdifferential in the definition, setting X_ε = {x in X : dist(0,∂Ψ(x)) ≤ ε}, and make the same correction in the repeated segment argument. Then exclusion from the r-neighborhood of X_ε places the relevant segment in U_ε, restoring the local model, inner-accuracy induction, and dependent convergence and complexity statements without changing the algorithm or any guarantee.
issues.why_classification: The old source’s earlier definition of an approximate-stationarity set, the description of X_ε as the stationarity set, and the definition of U_ε all uniquely force ∂Ψ rather than the scalar Ψ. The argument never uses objective-value distance under its literal meaning; the omission is merely copied notation. An intended reader can insert the uniquely determined symbol and continue without repairing any mathematical inference or construction.
